item.title: See How El Niño Is Washing Ashore in California
item.description: An enormous pulse of wave energy will soon reach the coast and continue north, raising sea levels by half a foot and increasing threats from swells and tides.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:description: A wave crashes into a sea wall protecting beachfront homes in Long Beach, Ca., where a boardwalk was damaged by Hurricane Marie.

item.title: As A.I. Panic Grows, Javier Milei Is Pitching Argentina As a Rules-Free Haven
item.description: Mr. Milei wants to go all in on artificial intelligence even as other leaders struggle to get a handle on a technology many fear poses existential threats.

item.title: AMLO Son Poses Political Problems for Mexico’s President Sheinbaum
item.description: Andrés Manuel López Beltrán has joined the list of figures who, critics say, may end up harming the left-wing movement his father founded, as well as the president who succeeded him.

item.media:description: Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, a politician and son of former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, at Mexico’s National Palace.

item.title: Trump’s Tariffs Push Canadian Companies to Look Past American Links
item.description: Shaken by tariffs and threats from the Trump administration, Canadian businesses are seeking markets and suppliers beyond the United States.
item.dc:creator: Peter S. Goodman and Alana Paterson For The New York Times
item.media:description: Since Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs in response to President Trump’s tariffs, the Canadian manufacturer Pacific Bolt has had to source steel domestically at prohibitive costs.

item.title: Brazil’s Biggest Election Question?: Donald Trump’s Next Move
item.description: As Brazil prepares to hold elections next month, Latin America’s biggest nation is taking steps to shield its democracy from potential American meddling.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Adam B. Ellick
item.media:description: Supporters of the right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro waved American flags and brandished a blowup doll of President Trump clutching an imprisoned President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at a rally this month in São Paulo, Brazil.

item.title: The Mighty Sparrow, Trinidadian Titan of Calypso, Is Dead at 91
item.description: He was sometimes described as the last of the true calypso singers. But in fact he simultaneously preserved calypso tradition and invented it anew.
item.dc:creator: Margalit Fox
item.media:description: The Mighty Sparrow in 2013. Known as the king of calypso, he was renowned for his sonorous voice, unremitting energy and the sly double-entendre that are among the hallmarks of calypso lyrics.

item.title: Carney Seeks New Trade Partners for Canada, But Knows the Limits
item.description: Canada’s prime minister is pursuing deeper trade, defense and cultural ties with China, India and the European Union, but none are likely to replace ties to the United States.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: As part of an effort to lessen dependence on the United States, Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada has signaled a pivot toward trading partners in Europe and Asia.

item.title: Haiti Turns to Roger Stone To Lobby Trump Administration
item.description: The Haitian government hired Mr. Stone, a confidant of President Trump, weeks after hundreds of thousands of Haitians lost deportation protection. The contract is worth nearly $800,000, a document shows.
item.dc:creator: David C. Adams
item.media:credit: Rebecca Noble for The New York Times
item.media:description: The political operative Roger J. Stone Jr. has secured a lucrative contract to lobby the Trump administration on Haiti’s behalf, according to a document filed with the Justice Department.
